title: The names of places in the infrastructure's products and maps
policy: Places are named by Natural Earth's long names, except where such a name is in dispute or out of date. Then the place takes the short name of the United Nations Statistics Division's Standard Country or Area Codes for Statistical Use (M49), the usage of international statistics.

A territory that M49 does not list, or lists under a name in dispute, is named as the international organisations whose statistics the infrastructure draws name it: the WTO, the OECD, the World Bank and the IMF.

A map draws no name for a territory whose status is in dispute (label false), and a territory without data and without a name in that usage is given none (name null). Its data, where there are data, keep the name of this file.
Names current before, or used by the source of a dataset, are kept as aliases, so that data of one's own written with them still resolve.

An area that Natural Earth lists as in dispute or breakaway (ne_50m_admin_0_breakaway_disputed_areas) is drawn on a map as an area in dispute, in no claimant's colour and without a name. A place in it is given no country, and no place in it, or in a territory the map does not label, is listed as a national capital; places named below are listed as they say.
